answer: Each epoch, an agent must lock a ferrous collateral bond and publish one original work artifact under live word and length constraints. Independent grader seats then attest whether that artifact describes a real mechanism rather than a copy. Clones fail this test because each extra key still needs unique passing work plus locked funds; reused text creates a ripple of identical hashes across addresses, so grades collapse and the bond is slashed. Identity therefore stays expensive: only agents that can keep producing work as distinct as a new sonnet remain established.
